topic: Nirma detergent from a bicycle beat HUL
title: How a government chemist beat Surf at a fraction of the price

facts.claim: Karsanbhai Patel started selling homemade detergent door to door in Ahmedabad in 1969.
Before that he worked as a chemist in the Gujarat government's Department of Mining and Geology (some sources say lab technician/assistant).
Nirma sold at about Rs 3 per kg while HUL's Surf cost roughly Rs 13 (sources vary: Rs 3 to 3.50 vs Rs 10 to 15). Use 'about 3 rupees vs about 13'.
The name Nirma comes from his daughter Nirupama (her death in an accident is reported only by The Better India / IMPACT).
Nirma reportedly passed Surf as India's top detergent around 1985, with an estimated share of about 60% (reported, secondary sources).
HUL responded by launching the low-priced Wheel detergent, reportedly in 1988 (single-source date; 'Operation STING').
By 2014 Nirma's detergent share was about 10% among roughly 400 brands (Business Standard, market estimates).
The Nirma group later moved into cement (Lafarge India for $1.4 billion in 2016) and in Sept 2023 bought 75% of Glenmark Life Sciences for Rs 5,652 crore (about $680 million).

lengthReason: It needs a setup (the price gap), a turn (Nirma passes Surf, HUL hits back) and a result (about 10% in 2014), which won't fit in one twist.
hookCandidates: A government chemist beat India's biggest detergent. With what?
One man went door to door and humbled HUL. What did he cut?
Surf cost 13 rupees a kilo. How did a rival win at 3?

lines.motionNotes: Hard cut, headline and cyclist on screen from f0, slow push. Punch at f100 on "With what?".

lines.text: A price. Karsanbhai Patel sold his detergent for about 3 rupees a kilo.
lines.voice: A price. Karsanbhai Patel sold his detergent for about three rupees a kilo.
lines.visual: BG: paper. TOP: generic packet drops in. CENTER: big counter 0 to 3 with rupee sign. LABEL: NIRMA, PER KILO.
lines.motionNotes: Packet drops in f0-10 with a small bounce; counter ticks up and lands on 3 at "three rupees".

lines.voice: Hindustan Unilever's Surf cost about thirteen.
lines.visual: BG: paper. TOP: generic blue packet drops in. CENTER: big counter 0 to 13 with rupee sign (about 13, Wikipedia / Business Standard). LABEL: SURF, PER KILO. Same layout as the previous counter so the 3 vs 13 gap reads instantly.
lines.motionNotes: Packet drops in f0-10; counter runs 0 to 13 and lands on "thirteen". No beat.

lines.text: He'd started in 1969, selling homemade powder door to door in Ahmedabad.
lines.voice: He'd started in nineteen sixty-nine, selling homemade powder door to door in Ahmedabad.
lines.visual: BG: paper. MID: bowl of homemade white powder with a scoop and plain packets. FG: strip of old Ahmedabad houses anchoring the bottom. Headline above.
lines.motionNotes: Powder rises f0-10, houses slide up f12, slow pull. Punch at f95 on "door to door".

lines.visual: BG: paper. Typewriter types the question; a bucket of foamy laundry rises behind it as the prop.
lines.motionNotes: Text types in on the narration, bucket rises slowly; calm beat before the answer.

lines.text: They did. Around 1985, Nirma reportedly passed Surf as India's top detergent.
lines.voice: They did. Around nineteen eighty-five, Nirma reportedly passed Surf as India's top detergent.
lines.visual: BG: paper. MID: golden trophy on a stack of banknotes, orange marker outline. Headline above; 'reportedly' as the sub.
lines.motionNotes: Trophy pops in f0-10 with a bounce; punch at f60 on "passed Surf".

lines.text: At its peak, it reportedly held more than half the market.
lines.visual: FULL-BLEED FILM SCENE (the one emotional peak, no numbers): photoreal AI image of a 1980s Indian washing ghat in golden light, bright white laundry drying, nobody facing camera. Short headline only, white captions.
lines.motionNotes: Soft entrance, slow pan right across the laundry; graded, grain, vignette. No beats.

lines.text: Hindustan Unilever hit back with its own cheap brand, Wheel.

scene.headline: HUL HITS BACK|WITH WHEEL
scene.sub: a cheap brand of its own

lines.visual: BG: paper. MID: generic unbranded blue packet cut-out. Headline: HUL HITS BACK WITH WHEEL (name in words only, no logo).
lines.motionNotes: Packet slides in from the right f0-10, light drift; punch at f55 on "Wheel".

lines.text: By 2014, Nirma's detergent share was about 10%, among roughly 400 brands.
lines.voice: By twenty fourteen, Nirma's detergent share was about ten percent, among roughly four hundred brands.
lines.visual: BG: paper. Big counter 0 to 10 percent, label NIRMA DETERGENT SHARE, 2014; small sub 'among roughly 400 brands' in the label.
lines.motionNotes: Counter runs and settles on 10 at "ten percent". Calm, no beat.

lines.text: Would you switch your detergent to save 10 rupees a kilo?
lines.voice: Would you switch your detergent to save ten rupees a kilo?
lines.visual: BG: paper. Typewriter punchline looping to the hook; coins rise as prop.
lines.onScreen: SAVE ₹10 A KILO. WOULD YOU SWITCH?
lines.motionNotes: Types out with the narration; coins rise slowly. Ends on the question.

upload.title: A government chemist beat Surf with one thing. What was it?
upload.description:
In 1969 a government chemist started selling detergent door to door in Ahmedabad. Within about 16 years Nirma reportedly passed HUL's Surf.
Sources: Business Standard (2014), Wikipedia, The Better India.
